(Photo by Elena COVALENCO / AFP) Content Share Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Bluesky Email Copy Copied Flip [ UPDATED: Aug. 28, 2:36 am , Kyiv time. Updating with Zelensky’s visit to Moldova, including his talks with Maia Sandu and Nicușor Dan and the latest on Russian drone incursions into Moldovan airspace.] President Volodymyr Zelensky arrived in Chișinău on Thursday to join Moldovan President Maia Sandu for the country’s 35th Independence Day, hours after multiple Russian drones violated Moldovan airspace during Moscow’s latest attack on Ukraine. The visit highlighted the increasingly intertwined security and European integration paths of the neighboring countries as Russia escalates regional tensions.It comes three days after Sandu traveled to Kyiv to celebrate Ukraine’s own Independence Day, where she awarded Zelensky Moldova’s highest state honor, the Order of the Republic. JOIN US ON TELEGRAM Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official . “Right now, it is especially important to stand together and strengthen one another,” Zelensky said in a public statement upon arrival. Advertisement “A few days ago, the President of Moldova was with us in Ukraine on our Independence Day. Today, Ukraine stands with Moldova on its Independence Day. Friends must stand shoulder to shoulder.” Five drones cross into Moldova The celebrations came hours after Moldova’s Defense Ministry said five drones had illegally entered the country’s airspace during Russia’s overnight attack on Ukraine. The drones crossed into Moldovan territory at different points along the Ukrainian border between approximately 4 a.m. and 6 a.m., according to the ministry. Sandu described the incursions as “intimidation,” against a backdrop of increasingly frequent Russian drone violations of Moldovan airspace. Other Topics of Interest Zelensky Receives Moldova’s Highest State Award as Regional Cooperation Deepens Moldovan President Maia Sandu awarded Zelensky the Order of the Republic whilst in Kyiv, as Ukraine marked its 35th Independence Day. The incident came two days after a Russian drone attack temporarily shut the Vynohradivka border crossing in Ukraine’s Odesa region, one of several recent Russian strikes on infrastructure connecting Ukraine and Moldova. Moldova’s Independence Day events included a military parade in central Chișinău involving more than 2,000 service members and security personnel, 150 veterans and representatives of partner countries, including Ukraine. Later in the evening, Zelensky addressed Independence Day celebrations alongside Sandu. Advertisement “I know for sure that together we will all be part of Europe – a free and peaceful Europe,” Zelensky said. Ukraine, Moldova and Romania discuss regional security Beyond the public celebrations, Zelensky and Sandu held closed-door bilateral talks before convening a critical trilateral summit with Romanian President Nicușor Dan. According to a joint statement, the three nations finalized enhanced coordination strategies aimed at intercepting and preventing regional drone threats , alongside boosting collaborative energy networks and transport infrastructure. “On the trilateral level... this meeting is proof that each of us has the maturity to understand the responsibility we have for the security and stability of this region,” Dan said. Zelensky pointed to Russia’s repeated attacks on Ukraine as a warning of the threat Moscow poses to neighboring countries. “You see what Russia has brought to Ukraine and what it threatens every one of its neighbors with,” he said, noting that Kyiv had experienced 11 air raid alerts that day because of Shahed drones and ballistic missiles. “We all understand how abnormal Russia is, and we must help each other so that any threats to our peoples receive a proper response.” Advertisement The three leaders discussed security and defense cooperation, with Zelensky saying Ukraine was ready to support the development of Moldova’s and Romania’s security capabilities. “Moldova and Romania are our natural allies in logistics, energy and many other areas,” Zelensky said. Ukraine and Moldova are both pursuing EU membership, while Romania, an EU and NATO member, has strongly backed their European integration. The tribunal ruled it lacks jurisdiction over the matter. Hungary was excluded from allocation votes after constructively abstaining from initial decisions. by Lidiia Osaulenko | Sept. 11, 2026, 11:01 pm Flip Share Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Bluesky Email Copy Copied EU and Hungarian national flags hang beside a classical stone statue on a building facade on May 22, 2009. (Photo by Flickr) Content Share Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Bluesky Email Copy Copied Flip The European Court of Justice has dismissed Hungary’s lawsuit against the EU’s decision to use revenues from frozen Russian assets to fund military aid for Ukraine. JOIN US ON TELEGRAM Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official . Budapest argued that the procedure violated voting rules as well as the EU’s fundamental values and constitutional principles, including the rule of law, the equality of member states, and the democratic functioning of the bloc. The European Court of Justice, the highest instance of the EU’s two tribunals, determined that it does not have jurisdiction to rule on the matter. “Consequently, this action does not fall within the category of actions which fall within the exclusive jurisdiction of the Court of Justice and must therefore be examined by the General Court of the European Union”, the Court of Justice of the European Union wrote on its website . Advertisement Hungary’s legal challenge is not over but merely delayed and transferred to a lower jurisdiction. While the General Court prepares to hear the case, the EU remains legally cleared to keep moving Russian asset profits to Ukraine’s military. The legal dispute stems from a previous EU Council decision. After freezing Russian funds in response to the invasion of Ukraine, the EU Council decided that the net profits arising from these immobilized assets would be directed toward supporting Ukraine’s budget through Extraordinary Revenue Acceleration (ERA) loan aid. As part of that original decision, the Peace Fund Committee was mandated to determine the specific allocation of the money on a regular basis. However, since Budapest had constructively abstained from the initial plan to use the frozen asset profits, the Peace Fund Committee ruled that Hungary could not participate in subsequent votes to allocate the funds – a procedure Budapest challenged as unlawful and which kickstarted the lawsuit. Hungary continues to block the opening of negotiation clusters for Ukraine’s accession to the EU. On Tuesday, Sept. 8, Budapest vetoed the opening of Clusters 2 and 3 for the fourth time. Advertisement The total value of immobilized Russian sovereign assets worldwide stands at around €290 billion ($339 billion), with the bulk held in a small number of EU and G7 jurisdictions. Belgium accounts for the largest share, holding roughly €180 billion ($210.6 billion) in frozen Russian assets, primarily through the Brussels-based clearing house Euroclear, which acts as custodian for a large portion of Russia’s central bank reserves. ecosystems for a competitive economy EduPro Summit #2: Relevant education and talent ecosystems for a competitive economy Economics News Published on October 16, 2026 By Magda Purice Facebook Twitter WhatsApp Linkedin Email Preparing people for a labor market in which technology, artificial intelligence and business models evolve at an accelerated pace, bringing education closer to the real needs of the economy and transforming lifelong learning into an essential component of competitiveness – these were the central themes of the second edition of the EduPro Summit – Education that Works, organized by AHK Romania, through its EduPro Vocational Training Center, on October 15, at the JW Marriott Bucharest Grand Hotel. The event brought together representatives of the business environment, the educational system and public authorities. “Vocational education and, especially, vocational education in the dual system represent a common responsibility. We will not make any progress if we limit ourselves to blaming each other. Each of us must assume a real, long-term responsibility and contribute equitably to the effort: schools and public authorities in the field of education, society and parents, but also the business environment”, stressed Sebastian Metz, General Manager of AHK Romania, in the opening of the conference. From school to career: education must be connected to the real economy The first part of the conference focused on the results and prospects of dual education, the transition of young people to the labor market and the skills necessary for the economy of the future. The panel discussion, moderated by Mihai Peticilă, co-founder of Edupedu.ro, had as participants Dalia-Maria Dărămuș, director of CNDIPT; Mirela Gligore, head of the Communication Service of the Sibiu City Hall; Laura Cârstea, director of the “Virgil Madgearu” Economic College Iași; Irina Manuela Butnaru, Penny Romania and Andreea Feierstein, Hornbach Romania. One of the conclusions of the debate was the need for a much closer link between the qualifications offered by the education system and the real demand for skills in the economy. CNDIPT (National Center for the Development of Vocational and Technical Education) has started the process of revising the approximately 200 qualifications in the dual system, in the context of the emergence of new requirements, including in areas such as green technologies and artificial intelligence. 10 years of dual education: from idea to impact This year’s edition also marked 10 years since the start of the School of Books and Crafts project, AHK Romania’s initiative in the field of dual education. In the 10 years, together with the six economic partners, Hornbach, Lidl, Metro, Penny/Rewe, Selgros and dm drogerie markt, 10 generations of students were trained in 13 partner high schools. Approximately 1,200 young people attended the dual system training, and more than 400 obtained the certification offered by the German Chamber of Commerce and Industry based in Berlin. During the event, the economic partners received a distinction as a sign of recognition for the successful partnership and for their constant contribution to the development of dual education. The future of the labour market: technology is changing. The ability to learn is becoming essential. The second major direction of EduPro Summit #2 shifted the conversation from the beginning in the profession to professional life: continuous training, reskilling and upskilling, leadership, talent development, wellbeing and organizational performance. The panel was moderated by Tudor Popp, Beyond Space and brought into dialogue Dan Lăzărescu, Bosch Romania; Radu Merica, RER Group and Mihai Strasser, Elite Architect. The message was clear: in an economy in constant transformation, recruitment is no longer enough. Organizations must develop their people and build a culture in which continuous learning and adaptability are part of the business strategy. “Today’s employees do not need strict specialization, but the ability to constantly learn and relearn,” pointed out Dan Lăzărescu, General Manager of Robert Bosch SRL, representative of the Bosch Group in Romania and Vice President of AHK Romania. Excellence in education and training, recognized at EduPro Summit #2 During the conference, distinctions were also awarded for concrete involvement in education and training. Bildungspreis, the award for Excellence in Education of the international economic network AHK-DIHK (German Chambers of Commerce and Industry Abroad), was awarded to Grup Feroviar Român, for its railway training project, GFR School. Also, Penny Romania received the distinction “This company trains in dual professional system”, a certification granted exclusively by the AHK-DIHK network, which certifies the compliance with German quality standards in dual training and represents a guarantee of the quality of the training process. Education that Works EduPro Summit #2 started from a challenge that is already affecting the economy: the shortage of people and skills can no longer be solved exclusively through recruitment. The response and the central message of the conference: relevant education and the economy cannot evolve separately. The skills needed on the labour market must be built through a real and shared responsibility of schools, companies, authorities and society. About the Romanian-German Chamber of Commerce and Industry (AHK Romania) Established in September 2002, AHK Romania is the official representative of the German economy in Romania and has over 700 member companies. Through the services it offers and the events it organizes, AHK Romania supports German companies in their entry into the Romanian market and is, at the same time, a reliable partner for Romanian companies interested in the German market. Through the Vocational Training Center, EduPro, AHK Romania is actively involved in training and professional development as well as in the implementation, development and promotion of the dual vocational education system, according to the German model, in Romania. Theme for 2026: Together for a stronger Europe. Trust creates tomorrow The Romanian-German business community believes that trust creates the force that develops companies, partnerships and contributes to the economic strengthening of Europe. A true builder of bridges between countries, markets and cultures, AHK Romania stands for reliability, continuity and trust. It is at the same time a platform and partner for companies looking for new directions and looking to expand. Through constant dialogue with the political, economic and social environment, AHK Romania creates stability, stimulates innovation and offers companies the opportunity to succeed across borders.
